problem: Retrieving evidence from large, heterogeneous, and weakly structured video corpora presents major challenges due to multilingual variability, noisy text extraction, and the need for robust cross-modal reasoning, with existing systems often overlooking spatial and cultural context like landmark reasoning (p.1).
methodology: The paper presents LLandMark, a modular multi-agent framework for landmark-aware multimodal video retrieval featuring specialized agents that collaborate across query parsing and planning, landmark reasoning, multimodal retrieval, and reranked answer synthesis (p.1). It includes an LLM-assisted image-to-image pipeline leveraging Gemini 2.5 Flash and an OCR refinement module leveraging Gemini and LlamaIndex to improve Vietnamese text recognition and visual similarity matching (p.1, p.7).
results: Experimental results show that LLandMark achieves adaptive, culturally grounded, and explainable retrieval performance (p.1).
key_findings: The Landmark Knowledge Agent detects cultural or spatial landmarks and reformulates them into descriptive visual prompts, enhancing CLIP-based semantic matching for Vietnamese scenes (p.1). Additionally, structured retrieval planning augmented with LLM reasoning enables interpretable, flexible, and culturally aware multimedia search (p.7).
title: LLandMark: A Multi-Agent Framework for Landmark-Aware Multimodal Interactive Video Retrieval*
